note: Tables defined BOTH by a runtime CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in cloudflare-worker/src and by the SQL tree, whose two definitions do not declare the same columns. D1 holds one table per name and IF NOT EXISTS cannot add a column to a table that already exists, so whichever runs first wins and a column only the loser declares never exists. WHICH SIDE WINS IS DECIDED BY PROVISIONING ORDER, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `migrate-d1 --bootstrap` loads schema_baseline.sql and then every post-cutoff migration, and branch-provision.yml runs it BEFORE `wrangler deploy` — so on any database this repo's own tooling creates, the SQL side lands before a request can reach a route and every runtime CREATE is a no-op. Only capital_calls and oauth_state_tokens declare a runtime column the resulting database lacks. That is why this list is a ledger of stale bootstraps rather than a list of live 500s. THE ENTRY TO WRITE IS THE ONE THAT NAMES THE MODULE THAT ALREADY OWNS THE COLUMNS, and this sentence replaces the one that used to close this note. It said resolving an entry means "widening the narrow definition", and three entries followed that advice into prose that recommended declaring columns a SECOND time beside the ALTERs that already owned them — which is the defect this gate was written to catch, recommended by the gate's own ledger. D192 struck all three. The order of repair is: first ask whether a module already declares the columns and can be awaited from the CREATE's own bootstrap, the routes/brand.ts:99 idiom; then ask whether the narrow definition is a duplicate that should be DELETED in favour of an exported one, as routes/monitoring_analytics.ts's admin_audit_log CREATE was; and only if neither holds, widen. A second declaration is never the answer. BEHIND-THEIR-OWN-READERS WAS SIX AND IS NOW ZERO. brand.ts, legalcap.ts, settings.ts, advisor.ts and monitoring_analytics.ts each bootstrapped a table and then queried a column that bootstrap did not create. Two were never real and the gate could not see why — it was file-scoped and forward-only, so it dropped every ALTER whose CREATE sat in another file or further down the same one. Three were real and D192 repaired them: settings.ts and advisor.ts now await the module that owns their columns, and monitoring_analytics.ts's narrow third CREATE for admin_audit_log is deleted in favour of routes/admin.ts's exported one. PARTNER_PROFILES IS NOT ON THIS LIST, AND THAT IS THE GATE'S OWN FIRST PROOF. D187's three-way collision is fully converged: routes/profiling.ts's 24-entry ADD COLUMN loop reaches migration 275's shape exactly. It appeared here as a one-column superset until the stale-entry refusal caught the cause — this gate's pair parser was dropping `['raw_chat_json', "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'"]`, because a quote inside a differently-quoted literal is content and the character class it used could not know that. The gate fails on NEW entries and on entries here whose definitions now agree, so this list cannot go stale. That refusal is what forced four lines off it in D192, and it is the mechanism that proves a repair landed rather than a claim that one did.
resolve_with: npx wrangler d1 execute studioos-db --remote --command="PRAGMA table_info('<table>')"

pairs.divergent:capital_calls: TWO INCOMPATIBLE SHAPES, AND ONE OF THE TWO CAPITAL-CALL PATHS IS DEAD. routes/legalcap.ts:73 creates (deal_id, syndicate_id, amount_cents, currency, lp_responses, notes, idempotency_key, created_by, updated_at); the baseline creates (uid, limited_partner_id, lp_investor_id, project_id, amount, paid_date). Neither is a subset. A fresh build carries the BASELINE shape, so legalcap.ts's nine columns exist nowhere — and legalcap.ts's own ten statements on this table name syndicate_id and lp_responses, so they throw. Already on record in sqlite-table-collisions-baseline.json, which reaches the same verdict from the mutual-fatality side; resolving it is a decision about which capital-call path survives, not a rename, and belongs to that ledger's entry.
pairs.divergent:oauth_state_tokens: THREE DEFINITIONS, AND calendar.ts KNOWS IT LOST — its own comment says so. integrations/oauth.ts:26 creates (state PK, user_id, provider, pkce_verifier, extra_json, created_at, consumed_at); routes/calendar.ts:105 creates (id AUTOINCREMENT, state UNIQUE, user_id, provider, expires_at, created_at) and then ALTERs expires_at in 'if the table existed in the integrations/oauth.ts shape'. The baseline is oauth.ts's shape plus that expires_at, so oauth.ts won and calendar.ts's self-heal is what production ran. The one column a fresh build lacks is calendar.ts's `id`, and NOTHING reads it: every statement across calendar.ts, fundSheets.ts, oauth.ts, salesforce.ts, carta.ts and docusign.ts keys on `state`. The one consequence the divergence DID have is fixed in this same change — see D191 and calendar.ts:130, where the sweep had been deleting every row oauth.ts wrote.
pairs.refused:project_metrics: A BOOTSTRAP REAL SQLITE REFUSES, SO IT HAS NEVER RUN. integrations/providers/stripe.ts:329 writes created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime("now")) with DOUBLE quotes; SQLite rejects that with 'default value of column [created_at] is not constant' whether or not double-quoted string literals are enabled, and the statement's own `catch { /* table exists */ }` has been swallowing the proof. Harmless today and only today: migration 249 and routes/progress.ts:1842 both create project_metrics with datetime('now'), they agree with each other, and a fresh build carries that shape — so the table the refused CREATE would have made already exists. Fixing the two characters is filed rather than done here, with metric_anomalies, whose sole definition fails the same way and which therefore does NOT exist.
pairs.interpolated:explorer_promo_codes: NOT ANALYSABLE, AND RECORDED RATHER THAN SKIPPED. services/explorerPromo.ts:75 builds its CREATE TABLE through a template literal carrying a ${…}, so no column set can be read from it without executing the module. The other definition is the baseline's. Silently dropping a definition the gate cannot build is how a gate comes to report a pass over a corpus it never read, so it is a finding kind of its own; closing it means making the statement literal.
pairs.superset:activity_logs: routes/partnernet.ts:99 bootstraps a five-column activity_logs (id, user_id, type, meta, created_at) while the baseline's own shape adds uid, project_id, action, details, actor, latency_ms, status_code, endpoint and method — the columns middleware/observability.ts writes on every request. partnernet.ts's own six statements name none of the nine, so it is narrow rather than wrong, and a fresh build carries the wide shape. It is a self-heal for a table that predates the migration set and has not been revisited since.
pairs.superset:cohort_cycles: A BENIGN SIBLING, and the two files split cleanly on purpose. services/cohortTiming.ts:177 creates the cycle row without applications_open_at, applications_close_at, app_status or force_proceed — migration 157's application-window columns — and its own ten statements name none of the four. They are ALTERed in by services/cohortApplications.ts's ensureCohortAppSchema, which that module awaits at :278 and which routes/admin_cohort.ts awaits at six sites and routes/spinout_lab.ts at one, covering every reader including force_proceed. One file owns the calendar, the other owns the window. A fresh build carries all four, and widening cohortTiming.ts's CREATE would declare them twice.

pairs.superset:landing_pages: THREE DEFINITIONS, AND AFTER D192 THE NARROW ONE IS THE ONE THAT READS LEAST. This entry used to say routes/brand.ts:42 creates 19 columns and reads 29 it does not create, and to call itself "the clearest case in the ledger for widening the CREATE rather than trusting the order". BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG, and the second would have written a second declaration of 29 columns beside services/landingPageSchema.ts's — the exact defect this gate exists to catch. brand.ts's ensureSchema awaits ensureLandingPageBrandKitColumns(env) at :99, after its CREATEs and before its memo lands, and that helper ALTERs all 33 in; the gate could not see it because its runtime side was file-scoped, which is what D192 fixed. brand.ts and migration 144 agree. What is left is services/advisor/writeRouter.ts:986, a 16-column CREATE for the same table — and it is BENIGN rather than narrow-and-broken: the only columns that branch reads or writes are `tagline` and `theme_color`, both of which it declares, and a database it reached first is healed by the same helper on brand.ts's own path. Its own comment claimed lockstep with brand.ts and migration 144 and was 32 columns short; that claim is corrected in place rather than made true.

pairs.superset:mvp_tasks: A BENIGN SIBLING, and the reason is the path rather than the column list. routes/pipeline.ts:41 creates mvp_tasks without `lane`, which migration 253 added for the board columns, and pipeline.ts's own four statements do not name it. pairs.superset:waitlist_signups: TWO HELPERS, AND brand.ts AWAITS ONLY ONE — which is why this entry survived D192 while landing_pages' half of it closed. routes/brand.ts:80 creates waitlist_signups without `audience` or the five CRM columns. `audience` is now accounted for: it is ALTERed in by services/landingPageSchema.ts, which brand.ts's own ensureSchema awaits at :99.
